key_insight: Proximity to a metal-insulator transition can be used as a tuning principle to expand optical transparency while retaining useful conductivity in correlated-oxide transparent conductors.
engineering_relevance: Ti-substituted SrVO3 shows that composition near the MIT can optimize the transparency-conductivity trade-off for applications such as silicon photovoltaics.
method: Use epitaxial Ti-substituted SrVO3 films as a model transparent conductor platform.
Tune electronic filling and disorder by varying Ti content to move toward the MIT.
Assess the balance of optical window, transport coherence, and Haacke figure of merit.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports a systematic broadening of the optical window into silicon-photovoltaic-relevant regimes, with the best performance occurring near the composition-driven MIT.
watch_item: Pushing too close to the MIT can reduce coherent metallic transport due to carrier depletion and disorder, so the optimal window is narrow.
paper_title: Engineering Correlated Transparent Conductors via Metal-Insulator Transition Proximity
